Notarial Law

Radboud University

← Back to search
About this programme

UCR currently cannot construct a sufficiently close programme for a meaningful curriculum comparison.

Notarial Law at Radboud studies the legal arrangements behind major life events and business transactions. It develops private, family, succession and tax law alongside legal research, civil procedure and the rules governing notarial work.

UCR offers useful foundations in comparative private law, business law, public law, accounting and economics. These courses do not sustain a complete programme centred on family and succession law, property transfers, notarial taxation and professional notarial rules. We therefore show Radboud’s curriculum without presenting a UCR programme as a comparable alternative.

Academic year: 2026–2027

External pathway: Ordinary full-time bachelor; criminology choice

The 180 EC programme comprises 175 EC of required study and one linked 4 EC perspective and 1 EC research essay. Criminology is the selected permitted pair; legal philosophy and sociology of law are alternatives. There is no open elective block. First-year tutoring participation is required without extra credits. The five-credit thesis has academic-skills entry requirements. Qualification for notarial practice and the regulated legal professions requires further legal study and professional conditions.
